candidate.title: SureCell™ WTA 3’
candidate.scope: Literal SureCell WTA 3′ product/library-preparation outline in the assigned Illumina poster footer: cell-containing droplets and bead capture through a cluster-ready 3′ mRNA-derived DNA library. The three colored examples illustrate barcode-bearing materials within one workflow, with no depicted alternative method or separate processing branch. Nextera is an embedded operation, not another assay target. This is a schematic-level architecture, not a complete protocol or a claim about all product versions.

states.label: Amplified library ready for cluster generation
features: The final DNA products are drawn as three paired-line examples bearing distinct Barcode colors.
Left-to-right in the drawing: P7 and Index region, cyan segment, transcript-derived insert, UMI, Barcode, Read1 segment, and terminal P5 region.
P7/P5 provide the depicted cluster-generation interface; the sample Index is distinct from the bead-derived Barcode and UMI.
The biological target is captured polyadenylated mRNA; the physical library/readout carrier is 3′-enriched, barcoded cDNA.

The intended expression readout associates transcript sequence with cell-associated Barcode and molecule-associated UMI. The figure provides no guarantee of complete transcript capture, full-length transcript representation or absolute recovery.
Actual sequencing and downstream data processing are beyond the depicted endpoint.

operations.label: Cell lysis / mRNA hybridization
operations.description: Lysis makes cellular mRNA available for capture. The depicted poly(A) mRNA ends hybridize to TTTTT capture segments on barcoded bead oligos, producing bead-associated mRNA–oligo complexes. The bead is a physical capture support, not a catalyst. The repeated cell/bead examples do not establish mixing of their contents.
operations.mechanism: Complementary AAAAA–TTTTT hybridization is drawn; the lysis chemistry is not specified.
operations.information_effect: Capture places mRNA next to the bead oligo UMI and Barcode within the cell-compartment context. Covalent transfer into DNA is represented by the following synthesis step.
